findings.title: JS client reads spec.family from /api/workbench/templates but compat alias is injected server-side — safe, but alias has no documented removal timeline
findings.suggested_fix: The compat alias spec["family"] = filename_prefix (service.py line 447) preserves the field the JS client reads. The contract is intact for now. A future commit that drops the alias (Step 11 comment in service.py) without updating workbench.js line 7008 will silently gate out all bundle actions. Enforce the alias-drop as a coordinated cross-file change and test it with the getEnabledActions path.

findings.title: workbench_save_session geometry validation moved before cell acceptance — clients that sent geometry-inconsistent payloads without triggering the old per-field checks will now receive 422
findings.suggested_fix: Previously, save-session validated anims/angles/projs after writing cells, and the projs check was only 'not in (1,2)'. Now _coerce_projection_geometry and _derive_session_grid_geometry run first and reject if grid_cols/grid_rows don't match the derived geometry. Any saved client that sends partial geometry updates (e.g. only 'cells' without re-asserting grid dimensions) could be rejected if the persisted session geometry now fails the new derived-geometry cross-check. Verify with a round-trip test: load a pre-existing session, PATCH only cells, assert 200.

findings.title: New top-level keys skin_family_scope and prefix_catalog in /api/workbench/templates response are not normalized/validated by _normalize_template_registry — they pass through raw JSON
findings.suggested_fix: prefix_catalog and skin_family_scope are passed through from the raw JSON without schema enforcement. The test test_template_registry_mounted_scope_is_explicit reads these sections directly. If the JSON is malformed or a future edit drops a key, the API will silently return incomplete data with no validation error. Add a minimal structural assertion in _normalize_template_registry for these sections.

findings.title: workbench_web_skin_payload response gains preview_normalized field — additive, but existing callers that assert exact response keys will fail
findings.suggested_fix: preview_normalized (bool) is a new field in the web-skin-payload response. Additive and non-breaking for tolerant clients. Tests in test_workbench_flow.py already assert it (lines 169, 474), so the new field is contractually documented. No action required unless a downstream consumer does strict key-set equality checks.

residual_risks: The compat alias spec['family'] = filename_prefix in _normalize_template_action_spec is the only thing keeping workbench.js getEnabledActions working. The Step 11 comment in service.py signals intent to remove it. There is no enforced coupling between alias removal and JS client update — a future commit dropping the alias will cause silent action-gating failure (all bundle actions hidden) with no 422 or console error visible to the user.

prefix_catalog and skin_family_scope pass through from raw JSON without server-side validation. A corrupt or partial template_registry.json update will produce a malformed API response. The normalization layer catches action-level missing fields but not top-level section structure.

The new save-session geometry pre-validation (_coerce_projection_geometry + _derive_session_grid_geometry run before cell acceptance) is a behavioral tightening. The deployed prod baseline may have persisted sessions whose stored geometry fields (source_projs, projs, grid_cols, grid_rows) are inconsistent with each other due to the old lax save path. Those sessions could now fail on the next save attempt with 422.
testing_gaps: No test covers the round-trip case: load a session created by the old code path (projs stored, source_projs absent), send a save-session PATCH with only cells, verify 200 (not 422). This is the primary regression vector for the geometry pre-validation change.

test_templates_api_exposes_normalized_contract (test_template_registry_schema.py line 1401) does not assert that spec.family equals spec.filename_prefix in the HTTP response — it only checks the in-process load_template_registry() result. A server serialization bug that strips the alias would not be caught.
No test exercises the getEnabledActions JS path against a mock /api/workbench/templates response that lacks spec.family — this would catch the alias-removal regression before it ships.
prefix_catalog and skin_family_scope structural integrity are tested only against known-good fixture data. No negative test for missing keys within those sections.
